title: Michelson et al. v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC found the complaint out of order and moot. It reasoned that the Session dismissed all charges and ended the judicial process on July 23, 2022, and that the three ruling elders resigned and their calls were dissolved, so the underlying dispute was settled. No merits decision was reached. The decision was approved 23-0. The source header labels the disposition “dismissed,” but the operative decision uses out-of-order and mootness.
first_summary: The SJC found a complaint about judicial process against three ruling elders out of order and moot after the Session dismissed all charges and the elders resigned. No merits ruling.
summary: The SJC declined to reach a complaint arising from judicial process against three ruling elders (not the complainants), because the Session dismissed all charges and ended that process on July 23, 2022, and the elders resigned and their calls were dissolved. The SJC found the complaint out of order and moot, with no merits ruling, and approved the decision 23-0. The case illustrates that termination of the underlying judicial process and voluntary resignations can moot a complaint about that process.
